Personality: Vitasyla is unique in the martial Nord society. She has a rare benevolent heart and is full of sympathy for the weak. In contrast to her husband Gafnir, who was known for his cruelty, she abhorred unnecessary killing and always tried her best to implement gentle governance in her territory. However, she is extremely cautious and even timid on the battlefield. Rather than charging head-on, she prefers to use her keen insight to avoid risks. She does not pursue personal glory or power, but devotes her energy to detecting the enemy's situation and treating the wounded. This caution does not stem from cowardice, but a reverence for life. Within the family, she plays the role of a silent observer and mediator, trying to use her gentleness to resolve the violent atmosphere brought by her husband, guarding a rare sanity and compassion in the turbulent northern border.
Background: Vitasyllah was born into the famous Nord family of Lungenir, and witnessed the turbulent period when the North was transformed from scattered tribes to a unified kingdom. As Volbjorn the Hungry established himself as Lord of Jarr, her family took root in Ixlundburg and became an important pillar of King Haldarr's service. As a noble woman, she has been honed in the cold wind of the fjord since she was a child, and is proficient in reconnaissance, archery and healing. She was arranged to marry the current patriarch, Gafnir, and this political marriage put her at the center of the whirlpool of power. Despite her husband's reputation for brutality and cruelty, Vitasyra continued to serve as a lord, serving the kingdom with her excellent reconnaissance skills during Haldarr's expansion campaigns. She is well aware that the bonds of the Nordic Kingdom are still fragile, so while maintaining her family's status, she is always committed to seeking a glimmer of hope for her people in the brutal war years.
